thread:
alex: noticed canary p99 host CPU spike ~2.3x this morning, short streaming calls worst
maría: flamegraphs?
sam: uploaded a trace (rv-1861119999) to perf dashboard
alex: quick top stacks: tokenize wrapper -> rust shim -> grpc::writev -> proto::parse_headers -> kvcache::evict_check
irina: grpc writev + parse_headers implies lots of tiny frames and HPACK overhead
cheng: we rolled selector v3 yesterday; it biases int8 for short seqs when batch<3
maria: yeah that selector change shipped to canary
sam: repro locally: enable selector v3 + streaming chunking -> writev calls double and host p99 jumps
alex: rollback to selector v2 + bump min_batch=4 on canary drops p99 back near baseline
perf-bot: regression alert closed after revert at 2026-03-23T13:05Z
cheng: hypothesis: selector v3 reduced GPU time per request but increased fragmentation -> more small writes, parse work, and kvcache checks
maria: mitigations: revert selector, throttle kvcache eviction, add micro-coalesce on writev when downstream latency high
sam: I'll open a small repro PR with harness + perf artifacts and add a canary flag for micro-coalesce
cheng: longer term: add host_write_cost to kernel selector scoring and simulate host-side costs in selector sim
irina: add observability for small-write ratio and writev latency so we can detect regressions early
maria: created INF-4823 to track selector cost-model + batching heuristics + kvcache tuning, assigning to cheng/sam
alex: good triage; if revert holds we'll do a short postmortem and block selector v3 until host-cost-aware scoring lands
